plain_summary: Stimulant laxatives such as senna and bisacodyl can cause stomach pain and loss of fluid and body salts, and may make bowel problems worse in an older person.

medicine_groups.name: Stimulant laxatives named in the list
medicine_groups.note: Tablets, drops, granules, suppositories and enemas for the bowel count. Senna is also written as sennosides or sennoside B. Coloxyl with Senna, Soflax and Sennesoft are senna with docusate, and pharmacy own-brand tablets of senna with docusate count too. Agiolax is senna with psyllium. Nu-Lax is a fruit laxative that holds senna. Docusate alone, for example Coloxyl tablets without senna, is not counted here. Macrogol (for example Movicol), lactulose and psyllium are not stimulant laxatives and do not count. Bowel preparation kits that hold sodium picosulfate and are taken once before a procedure, for example PicoPrep, are not counted here. Castor oil is sold under its own name. No Australian brand is listed for cascara or aloe. Skin products that hold castor oil or aloe vera do not count.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a Group A medicine (a stimulant laxative) is supplied to a patient aged 65 years or over. If age is missing and the other requirements are met, report only a possible finding and ask for the patient's age. If the patient is under 65, do not flag. One Group A supply of senna, sodium picosulfate, castor oil, cascara or aloe is enough. For sodium picosulfate, exclude a bowel preparation kit supplied for a single procedure, such as PicoPrep. For bisacodyl, count one course lasting more than three days. Use an explicit course duration or calculate days from the quantity and scheduled daily dose, respecting any earlier stop instruction. Do not combine separate short courses. If directions such as “as needed” or “as directed” leave the duration of a single course unknown and it could exceed three days, report only a possible finding and ask how many days it was taken. Report no finding for a course known to be three days or less.
cannot_be_seen: Use any dated observation about bowel habit or fluid and fibre intake and any recorded potassium or albumin result. Supplies alone do not show these details, the reason for the laxative or how often it was taken. Laxatives bought without a prescription or supplied elsewhere may be missing.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether the stimulant laxative is still needed, taking account of the patient's bowel habit and their fluid and salt balance.
